title.narrative: Strengthened legislative and policy frameworks for the protection of the rights of all workers including migrants and other marginalized groups

description.narrative: In South Africa, female workers continue to face high levels of gender-based violence and workplace harassment, creating pressure on government and labour federations to strengthen the application of the ILO Violence and Harassment Convention, 2019 (No. 190). Women also experience lower labour force participation, higher unemployment, unequal pay, and a disproportionate burden of unpaid care work. In response, the ILO, in partnership with labour service organizations, supports labour federations to review and strengthen their gender policies, aligning them with Convention 190 and other Equality Conventions to address systemic discrimination, and to better reflect current challenges and inequalities affecting workers, while promoting safe, inclusive, and equitable workplaces. The ILO also works with government to strengthen labour inspector capacity to detect and respond to workplace violence and harassment, and to support the development of prevention measures for vulnerable workplaces. In partnership with UN Women, the ILO supports the development of a National Strategic Framework for the Care Economy. Beneficiaries include labour administration bodies and workers, particularly women and other vulnerable groups. Although South Africa has adopted its fifth Child Labour Programme of Action, implementation remains constrained by weak coordination across government. Similarly, despite the adoption of the National Labour Migration Policy in 2025, enforcement gaps persist, leaving many migrant workers vulnerable and highlighting misalignment between law, practice, and international standards. In response, the ILO is supporting government to strengthen coordination mechanisms to address child labour, and to work with social partners to identify gaps in law and practice relating to Conventions 97 and 143 to inform policy and legislative reform. Target groups include children, migrant workers, and government institutions responsible for labour rights.
